unified_features.name: Ticket lifecycle
unified_features.rationale: A defines the statuses but cannot create a ticket; the user asked for tickets. Creation and statuses are two parts of one lifecycle, so they are one module.
unified_features.behaviour: An agent creates a ticket with a subject and a description; it starts open. Status is always one of open, pending, closed (database check constraint).
unified_features.improvements: Creation added at the user's request; A only had helpers for an existing ticket.

unified_features.name: Agent reply
unified_features.behaviour: A signed-in agent adds a non-empty reply; it is stored in order on the ticket with the agent's id and a UTC time. The status does not change (as in A). No email is sent.
unified_features.improvements: The real author is stored instead of the literal 'agent'; an empty body is refused.

unified_features.name: Close a ticket
unified_features.rationale: Only A has closing; its rule is kept as observed.
unified_features.behaviour: Closing an open ticket sets it to closed; closing a pending ticket is refused with 409 'answer the customer first'.

unified_features.name: FAQ content
unified_features.behaviour: FAQ entries (question, answer) live in a table seeded with B's entry; they are read-only in the app.
unified_features.improvements: Moved from a hard-coded list to a table.

unified_features.name: Suggested FAQ answers on tickets
unified_features.rationale: B's suggestion is the feature the user wants on tickets; it shares only the ticket text with U01.
unified_features.behaviour: The ticket view shows up to 3 FAQ answers ranked by the number of meaningful words shared between the ticket's subject and description and each FAQ question.
unified_features.improvements: Punctuation stripped, stop words ignored, ranked by overlap, limited to 3 (B matched any shared word, so common words matched nearly everything).
